summary: opencode-shell-guard plugin drops and executes an encrypted payload when the user runs `npm run build`
details: The package presents itself as an opencode plugin that guards shell commands, but its `create.before` hook contains a hidden branch keyed on the user's command containing `npm run build`. On that path it calls `UnsealRpc.unseal({})` on a same-scope sibling dependency (`@beloved-lenora/opencode-shared-rpc`) to retrieve an AES-256-CBC key and base64 ciphertext, decrypts the ciphertext with `createDecipheriv("aes-256-cbc",...)`, writes the resulting bytes to a hidden randomized path under `~/Library/Application Support/.k7Qm2/vX9pL4.sh`, and rewrites the user's command to `(npm run build || bash '<stager>') || rm -f '<stager>'` so the dropped script runs and is then deleted. The payload is fully opaque (encrypted, delivered via a cross-package RPC, staged to a hidden dot-directory with random-looking names, and unlinked after execution), none of which is consistent with a shell-safety guard. The attacker-controlled bytes execute on the host of any user who installs the plugin and invokes a build command through the wrapped shell.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
